lane: off-lattice geothermal structural emission (self-assigned; no externally assigned lane paragraph supplied for this session)
hypothesis: Concealed geothermal feeder faults (step-overs, relay ramps, blind volcanic-hosted structures) are systematically missed by the catalogue-adjacent dot lane (h19-5/D2.8/H33 family) and lie in the pinned 13GEMSDOE lattice's 3 px coverage holes; placing one dot per lattice-uncovered valid cell, prioritized by public geothermal structural favorability, targets unmapped faults while provably avoiding every prior lane's dots.
mechanism: Binary {0,1} dots at all 6,649 valid footprint cells that are >=300 m (3 px) from every dot of the pinned 13GEMSDOE lattice (sha256 b4570b40...), ranked by a weighted sum of public layers: USGS GDR Quaternary faults + SGMC faults (0.4), GDR Quaternary volcanics (0.3), GDR paleo springs + 2 m temperature probes (0.2). Weights sum to 1 so the structural score stays in [0, 1]. Binary emission on a fixed support follows the published DTI marginal algebra (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel).
named_non_fault_process: Erosional scarps, Lake Lahontan paleo-shoreline/terrace risers, lithologic contacts, and dike or flow-front edges can produce geophysical/topographic steps without fault offset.
